'''Alfred Jack Cole''' (1925 – May 30, 1997) was a professor at the School of [[Computer Science]], [[University of St. Andrews]] in [[Scotland]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Professor Jack Cole|url=http://www.heraldscotland.com/sport/spl/aberdeen/professor-jack-cole-1.394697|accessdate=14 June 2015|agency=heraldscotland|date=7 June 1997}}</ref><ref name="st-andrews biorgraphy">{{cite web | url=http://www.cs.st-andrews.ac.uk/~alb/cole/index.html | title=Professor Alfred Jack Cole | publisher=[[University of St Andrews]] | accessdate=March 12, 2012 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120218100506/http://www.cs.st-andrews.ac.uk/~alb/cole/index.html | archive-date=February 18, 2012 | url-status=dead }}</ref> He is credited with building on the establishing of the School of Computer Science at St Andrews.<ref name="st-andrews biorgraphy" />

== Career ==

Cole studied mathematics at [[University College London]], completing his [[PhD]] on the theory of numbers in 1952. He then worked as a lecturer at [[Heriot-Watt College]] in [[Edinburgh]] until 1956, when he moved to [[University of Dundee|Queen's College, Dundee]]. His interest in the potential of computer technology resulted in a move to [[University of Leicester]] in 1962, as Director of the Computing Laboratory. In 1965 he returned to Scotland and St Andrews, as Director of the Computing Laboratory and Reader in Computational Science.<ref name="st-andrews biorgraphy" />

From 1965 Cole devoted his next twenty years to establishing computer science at St Andrews. His innovative approach included pioneering the teaching of Information Technology to Arts students. He developed techniques for [[space-filling curve]]s to be used in [[video compression]], leading to his invention of [[murray polygon]]s.<ref name="st-andrews biorgraphy" /> One applied use of murray polygons is the [[halftone|halftoning]] of rectangular images without using [[dithering]] or [[edge enhancement]] methods.<ref name="visualcomputer 1991">{{cite journal | title=Halftoning without dither or edge enhancement | author=Cole, A. J. | journal=[[The Visual Computer]] | year=1991 | volume=7 | issue=5–6 | pages=232–246 | doi=10.1007/BF01905689| s2cid=5172526 }}</ref>

He initiated the ''Distinguished Lecture Series'' in 1969. This series kept costs lower than similar conferences, with the intention of exposing students and others to leading edge topics. Costs were reduced through industry sponsorship and support from the university's School of Computer Science.<ref name="st-andrews distinguished lectures">{{cite web | url=http://www.cs.st-andrews.ac.uk/distinguished-lectures | title=Distinguished Lecture Series | publisher=[[University of St Andrews]] | accessdate=March 12, 2012}}</ref>

== Jack Cole Building ==

To recognize his service, the school moved to the new ''Jack Cole Building'' in 2004.<ref name="st-andrews jc building">{{cite web | url=http://blogs.cs.st-andrews.ac.uk/alumni/opening-of-the-jack-cole-building/ | title=Opening of the Jack Cole Building | publisher=[[University of St Andrews]] | date=November 13, 2009 | accessdate=March 12, 2012}}</ref> This was formally opened on {{nowrap|1 July 2005}}.<ref name="st-andrews jc opening 2005">{{cite web | url=http://www.cs.st-andrews.ac.uk/~alb/cole/opening/index.htm | title=Pictures from Jack Cole Building Opening 01/07/2005 | publisher=[[University of St Andrews]] | accessdate=March 12, 2012 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120302002837/http://www.cs.st-andrews.ac.uk/~alb/cole/opening/index.htm | archive-date=March 2, 2012 | url-status=dead }}</ref>

== Personal life ==

Cole's interests included cats, hill walking, [[home brewing]], [[folk music]] (and [[concertina]] playing), golf, gardening and football. He was a supporter of [[East Fife F.C.]]<ref name="st-andrews biorgraphy" />
